- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a price spike (e.g., >80), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% for 3–7 day forecasts.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for 1–5 day horizons.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates in bearish sentiment periods; add 2–5% bias upward if sentiment <0.1 for last 5 days.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.0 within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.
